detail: ROS AgePeriodCohort census population estimates; one row per month/age with race-sex population counts across 46 columns, an aggregate population table with no sampled clustering unit and no response.

Aggregate national mortality rates (Age, Male, Year, Deaths, Population, Rate); one row per age/year/sex cell, no sampled cluster. births.Rmd fits no model. RULE GAP: age and period are structural APC dimensions, treated here as fixed rather than random groupings; could be read as an aggregate Deaths/Population panel if age or year were taken as a grouping.
Aggregate national mortality rates by age/year/sex (Deaths out of Population); one row per cell, no sampled cluster, no model fitted. Same APC rule-gap as the black-death-rates file.
Aggregate national mortality rates by age/year (Deaths out of Population); one row per cell, no sampled cluster, no model fitted.
Aggregate national mortality rates by age/year/sex (Deaths out of Population); one row per cell, no sampled cluster, no model fitted.

ROS Arsenic full Bangladesh wells survey (6510 wells); one row per well with Id and survey attributes, no village/community grouping column. arsenic.Rmd fits classical stan_glm(switch ~ dist100 + arsenic + educ4, binomial).
Stata source of the Arsenic wells survey (6510 wells, 57 columns); one row per well, no community grouping column. Classical logistic switching model.
ROS Arsenic analysis file (switch, arsenic, dist, dist100, assoc, educ, educ4); one row per well, no clustering column, as in the ARM wells example.

Raw Hamermesh/Parker teaching-evaluation source (463 x 64) from which ROS's beauty.csv is derived; same 463 observations as the registered beauty.csv. Carries profnumber (professor) and class1..class30 course dummies; the professor grouping is noted in the beauty.csv row.
Excel twin of ProfEvaltnsBeautyPublic.csv (identical 463 x 64 data), itself a duplicate of the beauty dataset registered as beauty.csv.
ROS Bypass example (age, severity, new, stay); one row per patient, treatment 'new' and length-of-stay outcome, no clustering column.

ROS ChileSchools regression-discontinuity analysis file; chile_schools.Rmd fits classical stan_glm(read92 ~ eligible + rule2 + ...). One row per school; the only categorical (cmb_regn) is a combined region with a handful of levels, a covariate not a sampled cluster (#23 area-factor rule). Subset of chile_full.dta.
Full ChileSchools source (6330 schools); rbd is a unique school id (one row per school) and the test scores are stored wide across years (cas/mat 88/90/92), so no in-table grouping.
ROS Coins coin-flipping demonstration (11 rows, 2 columns); a sequence of flip results with no clustering unit and no regression.

ROS Congress incumbency/vote data in wide form: one row per House district with separate columns per election year (inc86/88/90, v86/88/90), so the repeated dimension is columns, not a grouping factor (#23 wide-repeated-measures rule).

ROS Coop Riverbay election example; a wide table of cumulative vote counts per candidate across six count rounds (counts as columns), with candidate names as columns. No grouping factor in the loaded table.

ROS Cows dairy-additive experiment (BDA Table 7.5); one row per cow with treatment 'level' and milk/fat outcomes, no repeating cluster. RULE GAP: the .dat file has a two-line descriptive banner before the header that the whitespace loader read as string rows, so the loaded frame is all-string and mis-parsed.
ROS Death-penalty state table (34 US states, death-row and homicide rates); one row per state, no repeating cluster.
ROS Death-penalty poll support over time; a single stacked year/value poll series with no replication within a sampled group.
ROS Earnings example (height, weight, male, earn, ethnicity, education); one row per person, classical stan_glm of earnings/weight on height, no clustering column.
Wide twin of electric.csv: one row per matched class pair with treated_/control_ pre/post columns; the repeated unit is columns, not a grouping factor (#23 wide rule).

ROS Gay attitudes survey (81422 respondents; age, gender, race, three marriage-support items); gay.Rmd models support by age via a smooth. Only age/gender/race are present, no respondent cluster (state etc.) in the loaded table.
ROS HealthExpenditure country comparison; ~38 countries with many indicator columns (wide), one row per country, no sampled clustering unit.
ROS HealthExpenditure country-level spending vs outcomes; ~39 countries wide across 65 indicator columns, one row per country, no grouping factor.
ROS HealthExpenditure life-expectancy table; ~39 countries wide across 86 columns, one row per country, no grouping factor.
ROS Imputation Social Indicators Survey (1501 respondents, 15 columns); one row per respondent, used for missing-data imputation, no clustering column.
Wide raw Social Indicators Survey (1501 respondents x 943 columns); one row per respondent, no grouping factor.
ROS Incentives analysis file (rr_diff, value, prepay, gift, burden); the per-study differenced aggregate computed from incentives_full.txt (registered), with no study id column of its own.
ROS Introclass grades (midterm, final); residual_plots.Rmd fits classical stan_glm(final ~ midterm). One row per student, no clustering column.
ROS KidIQ variant (400 children; child test score, mother age/education); one row per child, classical regression, no clustering column.
Stata twin of child_iq.csv; one row per child, no grouping factor.

ROS KidIQ (434 children; kid_score, mom_hs, mom_iq, mom_work, mom_age); kidiq.Rmd fits classical stan_glm(kid_score ~ mom_hs + mom_iq). One row per child, no clustering column, as in the ARM kidiq example.
Stata twin of kidiq.csv; one row per child, no grouping factor.
ROS Lalonde observational job-training data (Dehejia-Wahba, 18667 rows); one row per person with treatment and earnings, a causal-inference example, no clustering column.
ROS LowBwt birth-weight logistic data (189 infants; low, age, lwt, race, smoke, ...); one row per infant, no clustering column.
Near-duplicate of lowbwt.dat (188 infants); one row per infant, no grouping factor.
ROS Mesquite biomass example; mesquite.Rmd fits classical stan_glm(weight ~ diam/height/density + group). group is a 2-level fixed batch, not a random cluster, matching the ARM mesquite exclusion.
ROS Mile world-record times; mile.Rmd fits stan_glm(seconds ~ year). One record per year, a single time series with no replication within a sampled group.
Variant of the world-record mile series (year, seconds); a single time series with no replication.
ROS Names auxiliary table (137 rows, two string columns); a name lookup with no response or grouping factor.

ROS Names frequency table (98148 names x ~134 year columns); name counts stored wide by year, so the repeated dimension is columns, not a grouping factor (names.Rmd fits lm(logcounts ~ years) on reshaped series).
ROS Names cleaned frequency table (98012 names x ~134 year columns); wide name-by-year counts, no grouping factor in the loaded table.
ROS Peacekeeping ceasefire-survival mini table (cfdate, faildate, peacekeepers?, badness, delay, censored?); one row per ceasefire/conflict, badness a 3-level covariate, no repeating cluster.

ROS Peacekeeping full conflict table (192 conflicts x 107 columns); one row per conflict with survival outcomes, a wide table (#23). RULE GAP: it carries undocumented 'cluster' and 'clust2' string columns that might index a grouping, but nothing documents them.
Older/wider Peacekeeping conflict table (206 rows x 268 columns); one row per conflict, a wide table with no documented grouping factor.

Pardoe's Academy Awards nominees, one row per nominee within a competition (Comp, 318 competitions): no .Rmd and no model; the inferred win column Ch takes three values (2 lose, 1 win, 0 for 20 rows) and PrW sums to 0 in most competitions, so no clean winner outcome is identifiable (the ros_b reader reached the same verdict; the ros_a row was refused by the merge as not binary, moved 2026-10-08).
